source.title: Preventing Gradient Attenuation in Lipschitz Constrained Convolutional Networks
source.authors: Qiyang Li; Saminul Haque; Cem Anil; James Lucas; R. Grosse; J. Jacobsen

record.tranche_reason: Uses gradient norm preservation to build Lipschitz-constrained convolutional networks and compares the resulting method's performance; it does not measure the training-error outcomes described in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports clean and certified robust accuracy, empirical attack results, and Wasserstein estimates. Those are not training classification error or training speed outcomes named by the versions. Figure 2 reports layer singular-value behavior relevant to gradient norm preservation, but that measure does not establish any listed version. The Wasserstein table is flattened, so method-to-value assignments are not recoverable with confidence.
record.test_reason: The study uses orthogonal convolutions and dynamical isometry to develop Lipschitz-constrained networks. Its results concern robustness, Wasserstein estimation and layer singular values, without testing the initialization-dependent training speed or depth in V4 or the outcomes in other versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors present BCOP as an expressive, efficient orthogonal-convolution parameterization that avoids gradient attenuation, report improved deterministic robustness and tighter Wasserstein estimates against their comparators, and acknowledge that it represents only a subspace of orthogonal convolutions.
record.recipe_differences: Trains Lipschitz-constrained convolutional networks with BCOP orthogonal convolutions and gradient-norm-preserving components; the paper does not use the classification-error recipes in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported singular-value behavior varies by Lipschitz-convolution method (OSSN, RKO, SVCM, BCOP).

fits_no_version.finding: OSSN and RKO drive many layer singular values toward zero; SVCM begins mostly near 0.5 and moves some toward 1; BCOP maintains them at 1 by construction.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The parameterization used to enforce Lipschitz constraints affects layer singular-value distributions during training.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorems 1–3 establish disconnected orthogonal-convolution spaces and show that doubling channels can represent all n-channel BCOP convolutions within one component of the larger parameterization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Additional channels can overcome a representational obstruction from disconnected components in BCOP parameterizations; this does not establish fewer spurious minima in ReLU teacher-student training.

record.problems: The singular-value comparison is qualitative and shown in a figure without numeric values in the text. The paper does not report the training classification error relevant to the claim versions.
record.rows_left_out: Clean and robust accuracy tables and empirical attack results were left out because they do not measure training classification error or the other outcomes named by the versions. Wasserstein estimates were left out because the supplied table is flattened and method-to-value assignments cannot be confidently recovered.

untested.parts: Training classification error, including fitting random or corrupted labels and effects of model size, stopping and regularization.
Spurious-minimum frequencies and the effects of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Depth-dependent training degradation, shortcut comparisons and the specified alternative training recipes.
Effects of activation-matched initialization on learning speed and trainable depth, including orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization and very deep plain convolutional networks.
Training loss and curvature relative to a measured stability threshold, including recovery, edge-of-stability dynamics and divergence.
Batch-normalization comparisons for training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparisons with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Statements about improved training stability rely on dynamical-isometry arguments without comparative training trajectories. Appendix F's qualitative observation of OSSN instability at high learning rates does not measure V5's stability threshold or recovery mechanism. Appendix O's incompleteness result concerns representational coverage, not the training outcomes asserted by V4.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, random or corrupted labels, model size, optimizer, and stopping.
Teacher-student widths, spurious minima, and gradient-descent outcomes.
Depth-dependent training error and residual-shortcut comparisons.
Activation-matched initialization, training speed, and trainable depth comparisons.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, loss rises, curvature changes, and divergence.
Batch-normalization speed or learning-rate tolerance comparisons, and Fixup comparisons.
